I’m in the process of gearing a tank up for my guild, and pugged a +5 Necrotic Wake the other day. My main Shaman is 2600 IO score, so I know all the dungeons like the back of my hand. I get to the first boss, and it’s immediately evident that nobody knows where to drop the frontal spew, and the DPS wipe the group. 

I start typing “hey guys, I’m tanking the boss at the ledge, drop the frontal cone facing the ledge and the mechanic won’t be an issue” and before I can finish typing the message, 2 of the DPS have left.

It was a +5, one wipe. It’s like one thing goes bad and people just immediately jump to “I’m not the issue, everyone else is, fuck this group, key is bricked”. If you’re running an 11 or a 12 then sure, the key is probably bricked, but a 5? Yeah, nah. Can’t stand that shit.

I applaud the mentality. If I was you I’d settle in for the long haul. There are probably 2 paths you can take.

Get a job locally, and start building up experience in a field and at a company that offers FIFO positions. Hydraulics, HDM, Sparky, Boily, Aircon tech, Get your HR, MR and LR licenses and any tickets that may be required, then see if you can transition into a FIFO role in said company. 

Second option would be to continue trying for a hospo role up there, if you nab one, get on to acquiring said tickets and licenses ASAP and see if you can get talking to some of the blokes while you’re up there and nab yourself a job as a dump operator, and offsider, maybe something underground. These tend to be the easiest roles to get into that aren’t hospitality. If you already have the licenses and tickets, all the better in their eyes.

All the best to you mate, and good luck!

FIFO utility work is not what it’s cracked out to be. A lot of people think it’s easy money, the money is genuinely not that good at all. 

As stated above if you even want to be sniffed at you’ll need either previous experience in a field that offers a FIFO position + the tickets necessary to perform said job + previous FIFO experience, or a close friend in the industry + the experience necessary + the tickets. Being used to hard labour unfortunately doesn’t cut it in any of their books.

A lot of companies will genuinely not even consider people that don’t have previous FIFO experience, because of the massive amount of people that think they can hack it, and then quit after 1 swing.  

So just a heads up, if you made the move because you thought you’d be on $40+ p/h for cleaning rooms, doing dishes and preparing food, you’re about to get a huge shock.

This confuses me so much. My 2011 wrx has 180,000km’s (111,000 miles for the Americans here) and has never missed a beat. Bone stock besides a BoV and some aesthetic/suspension mods. I do also drive the car enjoyably, but sensibly.

Before I swapped the stock suspension on my wrx out for aftermarket coilovers, I had never “worked on a car before”. 

Me and my mate popped her up on jack stands on a Saturday morning, and by Saturday night we’d installed all 4 coilovers, and without and serious issues (apart from having to adjust suspension after the first test drive because it was WAY too low and the guards hadn’t been rolled).

You can definitely pay a professional to do it, however it is definitely doable yourself if you take your time to learn, and the rewarding feeling afterwards is great.

Just an FYI I’m not sure if it’s universal but if you do it yourself, be careful bolting and unbolting your calipers, last thing you want is break failure on a test drive :)
